Class for fitting a double-standard sampling

Source: R/R6Class-networkSampling_fit.R
doubleStandardSampling_fit.Rd

A dyad is observed with probability \(p_0\) if it is 0, \(p_1\) if it is 1 (the vector of parameters is \((p_0, p_1)\)). Given the blocks, a dyad between blocks q and l is missing with probability \(m_{ql} = \pi_{ql}(1 - p_1) + (1 - \pi_{ql})(1 - p_0)\): the missing dyads are integrated out given the blocks, and the posterior probability that a missing dyad between blocks q and l is an edge is \(\nu_{ql} = \pi_{ql}(1 - p_1) / m_{ql}\), a Q x Q matrix. The parameters are updated jointly with the connectivity of the SBM (see SimpleSBM_fit_MNAR): this class only stores them, with the terms of the sampling.

With a single block, \((\pi, p_0, p_1)\) are not identifiable: the observed data only inform \(\pi p_1\) and \((1 - \pi) p_0\). The fit is then constrained to \(p_0 = p_1\), that is, to dyad sampling, with one parameter.

Super classes

networkSampling -> networkSampling_fit -> networkSamplingDyads_fit -> doubleStandardSampling_fit

Active bindings

df

the number of parameters: 2, or 1 with a single block (p0 = p1)

vExpec

variational expectation of the log-likelihood of the sampling, the missing dyads being integrated out given the blocks: \(E_\tau[\log p(R \mid Y^o, Z)]\)

log_lambda

Q x Q matrix, the log-probability that a dyad between blocks q and l is missing, the term of the missing dyads in the update of the blocks

blockImputation

Q x Q matrix, the posterior probability that a missing dyad between blocks q and l is an edge, with the current parameters
